text.p: ValuJet Airlines canceled all flights to Dallas and Fort Myers beginning Sunday, stranding about 3,000 holiday season travelers.
The Atlanta-based discount carrier said in a statement it no longer had confidence in the charter operator providing the service.
"It has become clear (the charter) is unable to provide the sufficient staffing and reliable service to which they committed," it said.
"This inability has resulted in significant last-minute disruptions to these operations."
Full refunds will be issued to the some 3,000 customers affected.
Valujet last week contracted with three airlines to fly passegers to Dallas, Fort Myers and West Palm Beach over the Christmas season up to Jan. 6.
The Federal Aviation Administration (FAA) had refused to allow it to fly the routes itself because it failed to prove it could do so safely.
Valujet was allowed to restart its flight schedule in late September after being grounded in the wake of a May 11 crash in the Florida Everglades that killed all 110 people on board.
Under an agreement with the FAA, it needs permission from the agency to expand beyond its current fleet of 15 aircraft.
The West Palm Beach run and all other ValuJet flights will continue to operate as scheduled, the company said.
